claim: The yeast Dsc E3 ligase complex has long been recognized as a Golgi-specific protein ubiquitination system.
source: The yeast Dsc E3 ligase complex has long been recognized as a Golgi-specific protein ubquitination system.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical understanding of the Dsc complex, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: The Dsc complex shares a striking sequence similarity to the Hrd1 complex that plays critical roles in the ER-associated degradation pathway.
source: It shares a striking sequence similarity to the Hrd1 complex that plays critical roles in the ER-associated degradation pathway.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on established knowledge about protein sequence similarities.

claim: Two novel Dsc subunits were identified using biochemical purification and mass spectrometry, named Gld1 and Vld1.
source: Using biochemical purification and mass spectrometry, we identified two novel Dsc subunits, which we named as Gld1 and Vld1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental methods (biochemical purification and mass spectrometry) described in the manuscript.

claim: Gld1 and Vld1 do not coexist in the same complex.
source: Surprisingly, Gld1 and Vld1 do not coexist in the same complex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F demonstrating that these proteins do not co-immunoprecipitate.

claim: Gld1 and Vld1 compete with each other to form two functionally independent Dsc subcomplexes.
source: Instead, they compete with each other to form two functionally independent Dsc subcomplexes.
evidence: This is supported by competition assays shown in Figure 4 and functional assays in Figure 5.

claim: The Vld1 subcomplex takes the AP3 pathway to reach the vacuole membrane.
source: The Vld1 subcomplex takes the AP3 pathway to reach the vacuole membrane
evidence: This is supported by localization studies in various deletion mutants shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The Gld1 subcomplex travels through the VPS pathway and is cycled between Golgi and endosomes by the retromer.
source: whereas the Gld1 subcomplex travels through the VPS pathway and is cycled between Golgi and endosomes by the retromer.
evidence: This is supported by localization studies showing Gld1 accumulation in VPS pathway mutants and retromer mutants (Figure 7E-F).

claim: The Dsc complex can regulate protein levels at three distinct organelles: Golgi, endosome, and vacuole.
source: Thus, instead of being Golgi-specific, the Dsc complex can regulate protein levels at three distinct organelles, namely Golgi, endosome, and vacuole.
evidence: This is supported by localization data (Figures 3, 4) and functional data showing substrate degradation at different organelles (Figure 5).

claim: Ubiquitin-dependent protein down-regulation and quality control are important for maintaining the integrity of all organelles.
source: Ubiquitin-dependent protein down-regulation and quality control are important for maintaining the integrity of all organelles (Arvan et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The ER protein quality control system has been well-characterized.
source: Besides the well-characterized ER protein quality control system (Ellgaard and Helenius, 2003; Ruggiano et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Other organelles such as plasma membrane, Golgi, endosomes, peroxisome, and mitochondria contain integral membrane E3 ligases or have adaptor proteins to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases.
source: other organelles such as the plasma membrane (Babst, 2014; Okiyoneda et al., 2010; Zhao et al., 2013), Golgi (Dobzinski et al., 2015; Reggiori and Pelham, 2002), endosomes (Fukuda et al., 2006; Léon et al., 2008; Nakamura et al., 2005), peroxisome (Platta et al., 2009; Williams et al., 2008), and mitochondria (Narendra et al., 2008), either contain integral membrane E3 ligases, or have adaptor proteins to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Two independent E3 ligase systems exist on the budding yeast vacuole membrane, each governing a different subset of vacuolar membrane proteins.
source: Focusing on the down-regulation of lysosomal membrane proteins, we recently identified two independent E3 ligase systems on the budding yeast vacuole (yeast lysosome) membrane, each governing a different subset of vacuolar membrane proteins.
evidence: This is based on the authors' previous research.

claim: The Ssh4-Rsp5 system selectively ubiquitinates a vacuolar lysine transporter Ypq1 to down-regulate the lysine import activity after lysine withdrawal.
source: The Ssh4-Rsp5 system selectively ubiquitinates a vacuolar lysine transporter Ypq1 to down-regulate the lysine import activity after lysine withdrawal (Li et al., 2015b; Sekito et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Zn2+ withdrawal results in the selective ubiquitination of a Zn2+ importer Cot1 by the Dsc E3 ligase complex.
source: whereas Zn2+ withdrawal results in the selective ubiquitination of a Zn2+ importer Cot1 by the Dsc E3 ligase complex (Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Rsp5 can work together with the Dsc complex to down-regulate a Zn2+ exporter Zrt3 when excessive Zn2+ is present in the cytoplasm.
source: Interestingly, Rsp5 can work together with the Dsc complex to down-regulate a Zn2+ exporter Zrt3 when excessive Zn2+ is present in the cytoplasm (Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Ubiquitinated membrane proteins are directly internalized into the vacuole lumen by the ESCRT machinery for degradation.
source: These ubiquitinated membrane proteins will be directly internalized into the vacuole lumen by the ESCRT machinery for degradation (Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The S. pombe Dsc complex contains six components: Tul1, Dsc2, Dsc3, Dsc4, Ubx3, and the AAA+ ATPase Cdc48.
source: Originally discovered in fission yeast, the S. pombe Dsc complex contains six components, including Tul1, Dsc2, Dsc3, Dsc4, Ubx3, and the AAA+ ATPase Cdc48 (Stewart et al., 2012, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: All Dsc components except Dsc4 exist in budding yeast.
source: These components, with the exception of Dsc4, also exist in budding yeast (Dobzinski et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015a; Tong et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Most Dsc components share sequence similarity to the Hrd1 E3 ligase complex.
source: Strikingly, most Dsc components share sequence similarity to the Hrd1 E3 ligase complex, a key player in ER protein quality control.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about protein sequence similarities.

claim: Tul1 is a multi-spanning membrane RING domain E3 ligase that is related to Hrd1.
source: Tul1 is a multi-spanning membrane RING domain E3 ligase that is related to Hrd1.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about protein structure and function.

claim: Dsc2, Dsc3, and Ubx3 are homologous to Der1, Usa1, and Ubx2 of the Hrd1 complex, respectively.
source: Other components, including Dsc2, Dsc3, Ubx3, are homologous to Der1, Usa1, and Ubx2 of the Hrd1 complex, respectively (Stewart et al., 2012, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Both Dsc and Hrd1 complexes contain the same AAA+ ATPase Cdc48.
source: Furthermore, both complexes contain the same AAA+ ATPase Cdc48.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about protein complex composition.

claim: The striking similarity between Dsc and Hrd1 complexes suggests the Dsc complex might play a role in protein quality control at the downstream organelles of the secretory pathway.
source: The striking similarity suggests the Dsc complex might play a role in protein quality control at the downstream organelles of the secretory pathway.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the sequence similarity.

claim: In S. pombe, the Dsc complex is critical to the proteolytic activation of the sterol regulatory element binding protein (SREBP) transcription factor.
source: In S. pombe, the Dsc complex has been shown to be critical to the proteolytic activation of the sterol regulatory element binding protein (SREBP) transcription factor, which is a Golgi membrane protein.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about S. pombe.

claim: Fission yeast Dsc complex localizes to the Golgi.
source: Consistently, fission yeast Dsc complex has been shown to localize to the Golgi (Burr et al., 2017; Stewart et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, it is generally accepted that the Dsc complex is a Golgi-specific E3 ligase complex.
source: In S. cerevisiae, it is also generally accepted that the Dsc complex is a Golgi-specific E3 ligase complex.
evidence: This represents the prevailing view in the field prior to this study.

claim: Tul1 was initially identified as a Golgi protein quality control E3 ligase through its ability to recognize and ubiquitinate an artificial folding mutant of Pep12.
source: Tul1 was initially identified as a Golgi protein quality control E3 ligase through its ability to recognize and ubiquitinate an artificial folding mutant of Pep12, which is cycled between Golgi and endosomes (Reggiori and Pelham, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Dsc complex is responsible for the ubiquitination and degradation of Golgi membrane protein Yif1 after amino acid starvation or rapamycin treatment.
source: Recently, it has been shown that the Dsc complex is also responsible for the ubiquitination and degradation of another Golgi membrane protein Yif1, after either amino acid starvation or rapamycin treatment (Dobzinski et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Arabidopsis homologue of Tul1, FLY1, is predominantly localized to the late endosome, instead of the Golgi.
source: However, the Arabidopsis homologue of Tul1, FLY1, is predominantly localized to the late endosome, instead of the Golgi (Voiniciuc et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Budding yeast Tul1 participates in the ubiquitination and recycling of an exocytic v-SNARE Snc1 at the early endosome.
source: Furthermore, Graham and colleagues recently demonstrated that the budding yeast Tul1 participates in the ubiquitination and recycling of an exocytic v-SNARE Snc1 at the early endosome (Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Dsc complex is responsible for the down-regulation of some vacuole membrane proteins in budding yeast.
source: Lastly, we observed that Dsc complex is responsible for the down-regulation of some vacuole membrane proteins in budding yeast (Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The VPS pathway transports vacuolar proteases such as CPY, Pep4 and Prb1 to the vacuole lumen via the intermediate endosomal compartments marked by the Pep12 SNARE protein.
source: The VPS pathway transports vacuolar proteases such as CPY, Pep4 and Prb1 to the vacuole lumen via the intermediate endosomal compartments marked by the Pep12 SNARE protein (Bowers and Stevens, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The VPS pathway is used to deliver ubiquitinated membrane cargoes to the vacuole lumen for degradation.
source: It is also used to deliver ubiquitinated membrane cargoes to the vacuole lumen for degradation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the VPS pathway.

claim: Some vacuolar membrane proteins, such as Vph1 and Ssh4, utilize the VPS pathway to reach the vacuole surface.
source: Furthermore, some vacuolar membrane proteins, such as Vph1 and Ssh4, also utilize the VPS pathway to reach the vacuole surface (Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The VPS pathway can be blocked by deletion of PEP12.
source: The VPS pathway can be blocked by deletion of PEP12, or the cargo can be trapped in an aberrant endosome (i.e. the class E compartment) by the deletion of genes encoding ESCRT machinery (Bowers and Stevens, 2005; Odorizzi et al., 1998a; Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The AP3 pathway transports a subset of the vacuolar membrane proteins such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP) from Golgi to the vacuole.
source: As an independent targeting mechanism, the AP3 pathway transports a subset of the vacuolar membrane proteins such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP) from Golgi to the vacuole (Figure 1A)(Cowles et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: AP3 pathway membrane proteins typically contain an acidic di-leucine targeting motif (D/EXXXLL).
source: These membrane proteins typically contain an acidic di-leucine targeting motif (D/EXXXLL, where X can be any amino acid), which can be recognized at the late Golgi by the AP3 adaptor complex for sorting into carrier vesicles that then directly target and fuse with the vacuole (Cowles et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Deletion of the AP3 complex leads to an accumulation of AP3 cargoes at the Golgi and forces them to traffick to the vacuole membrane via the VPS pathway.
source: Deletion of the AP3 complex leads to an accumulation of AP3 cargoes at the Golgi and forces them to traffick to the vacuole membrane via the VPS pathway (Cowles et al., 1997; Li et al., 2015b; Llinares et al., 2015; Odorizzi et al., 1998b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: At steady state, about 60% of the Dsc complex localizes to the vacuole membrane, whereas the rest appears to be on punctae that co-localize with the Golgi and endosomes.
source: At the steady state, about 60% of the Dsc complex localizes to the vacuole membrane, whereas the rest appears to be on punctae that co-localize with the Golgi and endosomes (Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Deleting VPS27 led to a partial accumulation of Ubx3-nG in the class E compartment, with a significant amount still reaching the vacuole membrane.
source: In contrast, deleting VPS27, which encodes an essential component of the ESCRT machinery, led to a partial accumulation of the Ubx3-nG in the class E compartment. A significant amount of Ubx3-nG, however, was still able to reach the vacuole membrane (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Vph1-mCherry, a cargo of the VPS pathway, was almost entirely trapped in the class E compartment in vps27∆ cells.
source: As a control, Vph1-mCherry (hereafter referred to as Vph1-mCh), a cargo of the VPS pathway, was almost entirely trapped in the class E compartment (Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B and citation to previous work.

claim: Deleting PEP12 only resulted in a partial accumulation of Ubx3-nG in the cytosol, with a significant amount reaching the vacuole membrane.
source: The same PEP12 deletion, however, only resulted in a partial accumulation of Ubx3-nG in the cytosol, with a significant amount of the protein reaching the vacuole membrane (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Dsc complex might use both VPS and AP3 pathways for its trafficking.
source: Together, these results suggest that the Dsc complex might use both VPS and AP3 pathways for its trafficking.
evidence: This is an inference based on the trafficking data in Figure 1B.

claim: APL6 deletion led to an accumulation of Ubx3-nG in the vacuole lumen.
source: Interestingly, although APL6 deletion did not change the punctae localization of Ubx3-nG, it led to an accumulation of the Ubx3-nG in the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis identified the 27 KDa band as Yir014W and the 31 KDa band as Ypr109W.
source: Mass spectrometry analysis identified the 27 KDa band as Yir014W (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, hereafter referred to as 014W), and the 31 KDa band as Ypr109W (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, hereafter referred to as 109W), both of which are proteins of unknown function.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: 014W-Flag and 109W-Flag can pull-down other tested Dsc complex components, including Ubx3, Dsc2, Dsc3, and Tul1.
source: As shown in Figure 2C and D, both 014W-Flag and 109W-Flag can pull-down other tested Dsc complex components, including Ubx3, Dsc2, Dsc3, and Tul1
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Vph1, an abundant vacuolar membrane protein, cannot be co-immunoprecipitated with 014W-Flag or 109W-Flag.
source: whereas Vph1, an abundant vacuolar membrane protein, cannot be co-immunoprecipitated.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Both 014W and 109W have four transmembrane helices.
source: Bioinformatics analysis indicated that both proteins have four transmembrane helices
evidence: This is based on bioinformatics prediction shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Both 014W and 109W showed a low sequence similarity to Dsc4 from several sequenced fungus species.
source: Intriguingly, both 014W and 109W showed a low sequence similarity to Dsc4 from several sequenced fungus species, including Stemphylium lycopersici, Escovopsis weberi, Tolypocladium ophioglossoides CBS 100239, and Ceratocystis fimbriata CBS 114723 (data not shown)
evidence: This is based on PSI-BLAST search results.

claim: 014W-HA and 109W-Flag do not co-immunoprecipitate with each other.
source: Indeed, as shown in Figure 2F, in a yeast strain that was co-expressing 014W-HA and 109W-Flag from their chromosomal loci, these two proteins did not co-immunoprecipitate with each other
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Each of 014W and 109W is capable of pulling down all other tested Dsc components, including Ubx3, Dsc2, Dsc3, and Tul1.
source: although each was capable of pulling down all other tested Dsc components, including Ubx3, Dsc2, Dsc3, and Tul1.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: 014W-nG localized exclusively to the FM4-64 labelled vacuole membrane.
source: Strikingly, 014W-nG localized exclusively to the FM4-64 labelled vacuole membrane
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 109W-nG only localized to intracellular punctae (~3.7 per cell, n = 110 cells).
source: while 109W-nG only localized to intracellular punctae (~3.7 per cell, n = 110 cells, Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Approximately 37.4% of the 109W punctae co-localized with the Mars-Sec7 labelled trans-Golgi compartment.
source: Further analysis revealed that ~ 37.4% of the 109W punctae co-localized with the Mars-Sec7 labelled trans-Golgi compartment
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Approximately 56.9% of the 109W punctae co-localized with the FM4-64 labelled endosomes.
source: while ~56.9% of the 109W punctae co-localized with the FM4-64 labelled endosomes (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 109W co-localizes with Ubx3-nG punctae as demonstrated by the RICo assay.
source: However, 45 min after the addition of rapamycin, FRB-mCherry was recruited to 109W-FKBP and appeared as punctae that co-localized with Ubx3-nG (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data from the RICo assay shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Deleting VLD1 eliminated the vacuole membrane localization of Ubx3-nG.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, deleting VLD1 eliminated the vacuole membrane localization of Ubx3-nG
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Deleting GLD1 abolished the Golgi and endosome localizations of Ubx3-nG.
source: whereas deleting GLD1 abolished its Golgi and endosome localizations.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Deletion of GLD1 resulted in a partial accumulation of smaller punctae in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: Intriguingly, deletion of GLD1 gene also resulted in a partial accumulation of smaller punctae in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Figure 4A and B), as indicated by its co-localization with the ER marker DsRed-HDEL (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: The assembly of the Dsc complex might happen at the ER.
source: This result also suggested that the assembly of the Dsc complex might happen at the ER.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ER accumulation observed in gld1∆ cells.

claim: Gradually elevating the expression levels of Vld1 can recruit more Dsc complex to the vacuole membrane.
source: As shown in Figure 4C, in a vld1∆ strain transformed with an empty vector, Ubx3-nG localized exclusively to the intracellular punctae. However, after expressing Vld1 using its native promoter, a significant amount of Ubx3-nG was recruited to the vacuole membrane from the punctae. Further increasement of the Vld1 expression level with a GPD promoter resulted in an exclusive vacuole membrane localization of Ubx3-nG (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Elevating the Gld1 expression level in a gld1∆ strain gradually recruited Ubx3-nG from the vacuole membrane to intracellular punctae.
source: Conversely, elevating the Gld1 expression level in a gld1∆ strain gradually recruited Ubx3-nG from the vacuole membrane to intracellular punctae (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Overexpression of Vld1-HA under the GPD promoter can displace Gld1-GFP from the Dsc complex, and vice versa.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, overexpression of Vld1-HA under the GPD promoter can displace Gld1-GFP from the Dsc complex, and vice versa.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Deletion of TUL1 blocked the degradation of both GFP-Yif1 and Cot1-GFP.
source: As shown in Figure 5, deletion of TUL1, the RING domain E3 ligase that exists in all Dsc subcomplexes, blocked the degradation of both GFP-Yif1 and Cot1-GFP.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy and western blot data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Deletion of Gld1 significantly reduced GFP-Yif1 degradation, whereas Cot1-GFP degradation was unaffected.
source: However, deletion of the Golgi/endosome-specific component, Gld1, significantly reduced GFP-Yif1 degradation, whereas Cot1-GFP degradation was unaffected (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy and western blot data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Deletion of VLD1 drastically delayed the degradation of Cot1-GFP without affecting the turnover of GFP-Yif1.
source: Conversely, deletion of the VLD1 gene only drastically delayed the degradation of Cot1-GFP without affecting the turnover of GFP-Yif1 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy and western blot data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Deletion of either TUL1 or DSC3 did not affect the locations of remaining complex components.
source: As shown in Figure 6A and B, deletion of either TUL1 or DSC3 did not affect the locations of remaining complex components, as demonstrated by Vld1-nG, Gld1-nG, and Ubx3-nG.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Deletion of DSC2 caused Vld1-nG, Gld1-nG, and Ubx3-nG to be trapped in smaller punctae that co-localized with the ER marker.
source: However, deletion of DSC2 dramatically changed their localization patterns. After DSC2 deletion, Vld1-nG, Gld1-nG, and Ubx3-nG were all trapped in smaller punctae that co-localized with the ER marker, DsRed-HDEL (Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–B)
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A-C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Deletion of UBX3 caused the accumulation of Vld1-nG and Gld1-nG as smaller punctae that co-localized with DsRed-HDEL.
source: Similarly, deletion of UBX3 caused the accumulation of Vld1-nG and Gld1-nG as smaller punctae that co-localized with DsRed-HDEL (Figures 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–B)
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Double deletion of VLD1 and GLD1 caused the accumulation of Ubx3-nG punctae at the ER.
source: Lastly, double deletion of VLD1 and GLD1 caused the accumulation of Ubx3-nG punctae at the ER (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6B-C.

claim: Dsc2 and Ubx3 form a core complex with either Vld1 or Gld1 to determine the subcellular localizations.
source: Together, our results suggest a model in which the complex assembly may occur at the ER, where Dsc2 and Ubx3 form a core complex with either Vld1 or Gld1 to determine the subcellular localizations.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the deletion analysis data.

claim: Tul1 and Dsc3 are not part of the core complexes.
source: Tul1 and Dsc3 are not part of the core complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the deletion analysis showing that deletion of TUL1 and DSC3 does not affect complex localization.

claim: Double deletion of TUL1 and DSC3 did not affect the proper targeting of Gld1-nG, Vld1-nG, or Ubx3-nG.
source: Consistent with this model, double deletion of TUL1 and DSC3 did not affect the proper targeting of Gld1-nG, Vld1-nG, or Ubx3-nG (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In the absence of Tul1 and Dsc3, Ubx3-Flag was still able to interact with Dsc2, Gld1-GFP, and Vld1-HA.
source: As shown in Figure 6E, in the absence of Tul1 and Dsc3, Ubx3-Flag was still able to interact with Dsc2, Gld1-GFP, and Vld1-HA.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Either deletion of DSC2 or the double deletion of both GLD1 and VLD1 abolished all the interactions between Ubx3-Flag and the rest of the Dsc subunits.
source: In contrast, either deletion of DSC2 or the double deletion of both GLD1 and VLD1 abolished all the interactions between Ubx3-Flag and the rest of the Dsc subunits.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Single deletions of either GLD1 or VLD1 did not affect the protein-protein interactions within the counterpart subcomplex.
source: Single deletions of either GLD1 or VLD1 did not affect the protein-protein interactions within the counterpart subcomplex (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Overexpression of spDsc4 under the ADH1 promoter allows Ubx3-nG to traffic out of ER in ~60% of yeast cells.
source: As shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C, overexpression of spDsc4 under the ADH1 promoter allows Ubx3-nG to traffic out of ER in ~60% of yeast cells.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Deleting genes encoding either ESCRT machinery (vps27∆) or the endosomal t-SNARE Pep12 did not affect the vacuole localization of Vld1-nG.
source: Indeed, deleting genes encoding either ESCRT machinery, as represented by vps27∆, or the endosomal t-SNARE Pep12, did not affect the vacuole localization of Vld1-nG, although the vacuolar trafficking of Vph1-mCh, a VPS pathway cargo, was abolished in both mutants (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Deleting APL6 resulted in the accumulation of Vld1-nG on cytosolic punctae and the vacuolar degradation of Vld1-nG.
source: In contrast, deleting APL6 resulted in the accumulation of Vld1-nG on cytosolic punctae, presumably the Golgi and endosome compartment, and the vacuolar degradation of Vld1-nG (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Vld1 contains a putative acidic di-leucine motif (233EITPLL238) close to the C-terminus.
source: Examining the Vld1 protein sequence revealed a putative acidic di-leucine motif (233EITPLL238) close to the C-terminus of the protein.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The acidic di-leucine motif in Vld1 is conserved among orthologues from different fungal species.
source: Fungal sequence alignment indicated that this motif is conserved among orthologues from different fungal species (Figure 7B) (Cliften et al., 2003; Kellis et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Deletion of the last six amino acids of Vld1 (vld1∆6AA-nG) caused a partial punctate accumulation and partial vacuolar degradation in wildtype cells.
source: This deletion caused a partial punctate (Golgi and endosomes) accumulation and partial vacuolar degradation of vld1∆6AA-nG in wildtype cells (Figure 7C)
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Deletion of PEP12 completely blocked the vld1∆6AA-nG trafficking and the protein appeared as numerous tiny 'cytosolic' punctae outside the vacuole.
source: Further deletion of the PEP12 gene, which eliminates the VPS pathway, completely blocked the vld1∆6AA-nG trafficking and the protein appeared as numerous tiny 'cytosolic' punctae outside the vacuole (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A single E233 to A233 mutation (vld1E233A-nG) was sufficient to cause trafficking defects similar to vld1∆6AA-nG.
source: As shown in Figure 7D, a single E233 to A233 mutation (vld1E233A-nG) was sufficient to cause trafficking defects similar to vld1∆6AA–nG.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: A fraction of the Gld1-nG punctae co-localized with the Vph1-mCherry labelled class E compartment in vps27∆ strain.
source: As shown in Figure 7E, a fraction of the Gld1-nG punctae co-localized with the Vph1-mCherry labelled class E compartment in vps27∆ strain.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: In the pep12∆ strain, Gld1-nG trafficking was disrupted and the protein appeared as 'cytosolic', with very few punctae left.
source: In the pep12∆ strain, Gld1-nG trafficking was also disrupted and the protein appeared as 'cytosolic', with very few punctae left.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Deleting VPS35 resulted in the mis-localization of Gld1-nG to the vacuole membrane.
source: As shown in Figure 7F, deleting VPS35, an essential subunit in the retromer complex, resulted in the mis-localization of Gld1-nG to the vacuole membrane.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The human proteome contains approximately 19,000-20,000 different proteins.
source: For example, the human proteome contains ~19,000–20,000 different proteins (Kim et al., 2014; Wilhelm et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The human proteome has approximately 640 E3 ligases.
source: but only has ~640 E3 ligases (Morreale and Walden, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The human proteome has 6,000-7,000 predicted transmembrane proteins.
source: The human proteome has 6,000–7,000 predicted transmembrane proteins.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the human proteome.

claim: There are only approximately 50 predicted transmembrane E3 ligases in the human proteome.
source: However, there are only ~50 predicted transmembrane E3 ligases (Lussier et al., 2012; Nakamura, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: One strategy to expand E3 ligase substrate repertoire is through the expansion of interchangeable F-box proteins in the SCF E3 ligase complex.
source: At the protein level, one strategy is through the expansion of the interchangeable F-box proteins in the SCF E3 ligase complex.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about SCF complexes.

claim: F-box is an approximately 50 amino acids motif that mediates protein-protein interaction.
source: F-box is an approximately 50 amino acids motif that mediates protein-protein interaction (Kipreos and Pagano, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Budding yeast has only 11 F-box proteins.
source: For example, although budding yeast has only 11 F-box proteins
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about yeast.

claim: C. elegans has more than 300 F-box proteins.
source: C. elegans has more than 300 F-box proteins (Kipreos and Pagano, 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: A. thaliana has over 1,300 F-box proteins.
source: and A. thaliana has over 1,300 F-box proteins (Hua et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Another strategy to expand E3 ligase substrate repertoire is to use adaptor proteins to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases to different organelle surfaces.
source: At the organelle level, another strategy is to use adaptor proteins to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases to different organelle surface.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about E3 ligase recruitment mechanisms.

claim: In budding yeast, the NEDD4 family E3 ligase Rsp5 can be recruited to the plasma membrane, Golgi, endosomes, and vacuole by different PY motif containing proteins.
source: For example, in budding yeast, the NEDD4 family E3 ligase Rsp5 can be recruited to the plasma membrane (Lin et al., 2008; MacGurn et al., 2012), Golgi (Hettema et al., 2004), endosomes (Léon et al., 2008), and vacuole (Li et al., 2015b) by different PY motif containing proteins (Wang et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The PY motif interacts with the WW motifs of Rsp5 to recruit the ligase.
source: The PY motif interacts with the WW motifs of Rsp5 to recruit the ligase.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about Rsp5 recruitment.

claim: A similar recruitment mechanism has been observed for the human NEDD4 family members.
source: A similar recruitment mechanism has been observed for the human NEDD4 family members.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about human NEDD4 proteins.

claim: The human NEDD4-2 can be recruited to the plasma membrane by the PY motif within the surface epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) protein in order to down-regulate ENaC.
source: The human NEDD4-2 can be recruited to the plasma membrane by the PY motif within the surface epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) protein in order to down-regulate ENaC (Fotia et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Both VPS and AP3 pathways are conserved from yeast to human.
source: Because both VPS and AP3 pathways are conserved from yeast to human (Bonifacino and Traub, 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Human cells might use a similar strategy to expand the substrate repertoire of their membrane E3 ligases.
source: it is reasonable to speculate that human cells might use a similar strategy to expand the substrate repertoire of their membrane E3 ligases.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on pathway conservation.

claim: Several human RING domain E3 ligases have been identified in the endomembrane trafficking pathways, such as March2, March3, March11, RNF152, and RNF167.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, several human RING domain E3 ligases have been identified in the endomembrane trafficking pathways, such as March2, March3, March11, RNF152, and RNF167 (Deng et al., 2015; Lussier et al., 2012; Nakamura, 2011; Nakamura et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Endosomes are intermediate transporting organelles between the Golgi (or plasma membrane for endocytosis) and lysosomes.
source: Endosomes are intermediate transporting organelles between the Golgi (or plasma membrane for endocytosis) and lysosomes.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about endosome function.

claim: On the endosome, ubiquitinated membrane cargoes are sorted and internalized into the lumen as intraluminal vesicles by the ESCRT machinery.
source: On the endosome, ubiquitinated membrane cargoes are sorted and internalized into the lumen as intraluminal vesicles by the ESCRT machinery
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about ESCRT function.

claim: Cargo receptors such as LDL receptor in human and Vps10 in yeast are recycled back to either plasma membrane or Golgi.
source: whereas cargo receptors such as LDL receptor in human and Vps10 in yeast will be recycled back to either plasma membrane or Golgi (Goldstein and Brown, 2009; Seaman et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Many studies have reported that endosomes contain E3 ligase systems in yeast, plants, and metazoans.
source: As stated above, many studies have reported that endosomes also contain E3 ligase systems in yeast, plants, and metazoans (Léon et al., 2008; Nakamura, 2011; Tian et al., 2015; Voiniciuc et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: One hypothesis for the function of endosomal E3 ligases is to counteract the activity of endosomal deubiquitinases (Dubs).
source: One reasonable hypothesis is to counteract the activity of endosomal deubiquitinases (Dubs) (Kee et al., 2005; Kee et al., 2006; Léon et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: During endomembrane trafficking, ubiquitinated cargoes can be deubiquitinated by the Dubs and later recycled by the retromer.
source: During the endomembrane trafficking, ubiquitinated cargoes can be deubiquitinated by the Dubs and later recycled by the retromer.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cargo recycling.

claim: The presence of endosomal E3 ligases enables the cell to determine whether a cargo needs to be degraded or recycled at the endosome stage.
source: The presence of endosomal E3 ligases enables the cell to have the capability of determining whether a cargo needs to be degraded or recycled at the endosome stage (Léon et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Vld1-containing Dsc subcomplex, when forced into the VPS pathway, was recognized by an unidentified endosomal protein quality control (EQC) system and degraded inside the vacuole lumen.
source: In this study, we made a surprising observation that the Vld1-containing Dsc subcomplex, when forced into the VPS pathway, was recognized by an unidentified endosomal protein quality control (EQC) system and degraded inside the vacuole lumen (Figures 1B and 7A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figures 1B and 7A.

claim: This observation indicated that endosomal E3 ligases may have the capability of recognizing mislocalized proteins and removing them.
source: This observation indicated that endosomal E3 ligases may indeed have the capability of recognizing mislocalized proteins and removing them
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of Vld1 degradation.

claim: The only difference between the two Dsc subcomplexes were the Vld1 and Gld1 subunits, which are homologous to each other.
source: Strikingly, the only difference between the two subcomplexes were the Vld1 and Gld1 subunits, which are homologous to each other.
evidence: This is based on the experimental data showing complex composition.

claim: The EQC system was able to recognize Vld1 and selectively ubiquitinate the protein.
source: Yet, the EQC system was able to recognize Vld1 and selectively ubiquitinate the protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the selective degradation of Vld1 in the apl6∆ mutant.

claim: Ubx3 forms a stable complex with the rest of the Dsc components.
source: We chose Ubx3 to represent the Dsc complex because: (1) Ubx3 forms a stable complex with the rest of the Dsc components.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: Antibody-mediated depletion of Ubx3 almost completely depletes the entire Dsc complex from the cell lysate.
source: Antibody-mediated depletion of Ubx3 almost completely depletes the entire Dsc complex from the cell lysate
evidence: This is based on the authors' experimental observations.

claim: Ubx3 is the only Dsc component that can be chromosomally tagged with fluorescent proteins without abolishing Dsc function in budding yeast.
source: (2) Ubx3 is the only Dsc component that can be chromosomally tagged with fluorescent proteins without abolishing Dsc function in budding yeast (Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: mNeonGreen is a green fluorescent protein that is similar to GFP in size, but about two times brighter than GFP.
source: To begin the investigation, we tagged Ubx3 with mNeonGreen, a green fluorescent protein that is similar to GFP in size, but about two times brighter than GFP (Shaner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In the wild type strain, Ubx3-mNeonGreen localized to the vacuole membrane and intracellular punctae.
source: In the wild type strain, Ubx3-mNeonGreen (hereafter referred to as Ubx3-nG) localized to the vacuole membrane and intracellular punctae, consistent with our previous observation (Figure 1B)(Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Dsc complex containing Ubx3-Flag is still able to ubiquitinate a vacuole membrane substrate Cot1 after Zn2+ withdrawal.
source: Our previous research has demonstrated that the Dsc complex containing Ubx3-Flag is still able to ubiquitinate a vacuole membrane substrate Cot1 after Zn2+ withdrawal (Li et al., 2015a)
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: All known components of the budding yeast Dsc complex, including Dsc2, Dsc3, Tul1, and Cdc48, can be co-purified with Ubx3-Flag.
source: As shown in Figure 2A–B, all known components of the budding yeast Dsc complex, including Dsc2, Dsc3, Tul1, and Cdc48, can be co-purified with Ubx3-Flag.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Two new bands at ~27 and ~31 KDa co-immunoprecipitated with Ubx3-Flag.
source: Importantly, two new bands at ~27 and ~31 KDa, respectively, co-immunoprecipitated with Ubx3-Flag.
evidence: This is supported by silver staining data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Yir014W and Ypr109W are proteins of unknown function.
source: Mass spectrometry analysis identified the 27 KDa band as Yir014W (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, hereafter referred to as 014W), and the 31 KDa band as Ypr109W (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, hereafter referred to as 109W), both of which are proteins of unknown function.
evidence: This is based on the lack of functional annotation for these proteins.

claim: 014W and 109W might be the 'missing' Dsc4 in budding yeast.
source: suggesting they might be the 'missing' Dsc4 in budding yeast.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on sequence similarity to Dsc4.

claim: The distinct localizations of 109W and 014W are consistent with a model in which these two proteins form distinct subcomplexes that travel separately to either the Golgi/endosome or the vacuole membrane.
source: The distinct localizations of 109W and 014W are consistent with a model in which these two proteins form distinct subcomplexes that travel separately to either the Golgi/endosome or the vacuole membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on the localization data.

claim: Ubx3-nG, Vld1-nG, and Gld1-nG are still functional because they can support the degradation of both Cot1-GFP and GFP-Yif1.
source: All three tagged proteins are still functional because they can support the degradation of both Cot1-GFP and GFP-Yif1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The two core complexes determine the subcellular localizations of the Dsc complex.
source: With our analysis, we now know the core complex should also include either Vld1 or Gld1, and more importantly, the two core complexes determine the subcellular localizations of the Dsc complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the deletion and IP analysis.

claim: The putative acidic di-leucine motif is important for the trafficking of Vld1 through the AP3 pathway.
source: All together, these results strongly indicate that the putative acidic di-leucine motif is important for the trafficking of Vld1 through the AP3 pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data shown in Figure 7C-D.

claim: The Dsc subcomplexes use two independent trafficking pathways for their subcellular localizations.
source: Taken together, we conclude that the Dsc subcomplexes use two independent trafficking pathways for their subcellular localizations.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the trafficking data in Figure 7.

claim: This novel mechanism enables the cell to achieve protein regulation and probably quality control at three distinct organelles using just one RING domain E3 ligase Tul1.
source: This mechanism allows the cell to achieve protein regulation and probably quality control at three distinct organelles, namely Golgi, endosomes, and vacuole, using just one RING domain E3 ligase Tul1 (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.
